# A const whose initializer reads itself does not take the compiler down.
#
# `evalIdent` reads a const's value by evaluating its initializer, and the
# initializer reads the const: evalIdent <-> evalExpr with nothing between
# them. `const a int = a` was a one-line program that ended in
#
#   runtime: goroutine stack exceeds 1000000000-byte limit
#   fatal error: stack overflow
#
# with no position and no message. Pre-existing, and found from the other end:
# the identical shape in a window prop (window_prop_reads_itself.txt) needed
# the same guard, keyed the same way, twenty lines away.
#
# Answered "not constant", which leaves the initializer standing -- what a
# const the optimizer cannot evaluate already does. Survivable rather than
# right, and the page says exactly how much so: the self-reference reaches the
# output verbatim as `var a = a`, and the span that reads it renders empty --
# the element survives, its content does not, and the page carries no
# initializer to fill it. No diagnostic either way.
#
# That `var a = a` is tolerable at all is a fact about the JavaScript emitter,
# not about this guard: `var` hoists, so the line assigns undefined to itself
# and the page loads. Spelled `let` or `const` the identical line is a TDZ
# ReferenceError and the page breaks outright -- which would turn a silently
# missing value into a broken one and make leaving the expression standing the
# wrong trade. The two denies below are what would notice.
#
# The rule that a declaration may not read itself belongs in the checker, and
# this is why a guard here cannot be the answer: `sngl check` accepts this
# program and always did, because the checker never folds. CLAUDE.md says so
# and this fixture is what changing it would update.
#
# A CLI script rather than a golden because the first thing asserted is that
# the compiler comes back at all.
sngl generate --lang none --platform html --out out selfconst.sngl
grep '<title>t</title>' out/index.html
grep 'var a = a;' out/index.html
! grep '__sngl_init' out/index.html
! grep 'let a = a' out/index.html
! grep 'const a = a' out/index.html

# A cycle reaches the guard by a second key rather than the first one twice.
sngl generate --lang none --platform html --out out2 cycle.sngl
grep '<title>t</title>' out2/index.html
grep 'var a = b;' out2/index.html
grep 'var b = a;' out2/index.html

-- selfconst.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"

output {
    none {
        html
    }
}

const a int = a

window #home(title="t", href="/index.html") {
    text(value="{a}")
}
-- cycle.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"

output {
    none {
        html
    }
}

const a int = b
const b int = a

window #home(title="t", href="/index.html") {
    text(value="{a}")
}
